items.title: An omega-categorical supersimple theory whose fibre dimension strictly exceeds the non-minimality degree
items.author: John Baldwin, James Freitag, Scott Mutchnik
authors: John Baldwin, James Freitag, Scott Mutchnik
items.work: Simple Homogeneous Structures and Indiscernible Sequence Invariants
items.difficulty_reason: The theorem exhibits, for every n, an omega-categorical supersimple theory with a type whose fibre dimension strictly exceeds its non-minimality degree, the degree being exactly n (statement lines 1749-1754). The proof instantiates the same generic construction as the earlier existence result but with a piecewise f whose simplicity criteria only hold from n+2 onwards, so the finitely many amalgamation instances involving small structures have to be checked individually following the cited remark (proof lines 1758-1769). The two steps that carry the content are then the computation nmdeg(p) = n, which combines the rank with a predimension obstruction to the algebraic closure of n points having size n+1, and the strict inequality F_ind(p) > n, where the indiscernible-sequence analysis splits into the case where all (n+1)-tuples satisfy the relation - impossible because long sequences would have negative predimension - and the case where none does (proof lines 1769-1814). Both estimates are quantitative and are the substance of the proof. H2.
